case_title: SUNIL v. STATE OF NCT OF DELHI
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Arms Act s.27
aggravating_circumstances: Indiscriminate firing resulting in multiple deaths and injuries
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Sections 302 and 307 read with Section 34 IPC
neutral_facts: The accused, along with others, were involved in a dispute with another family over an incident of eve-teasing. During the altercation, the main accused fired gunshots from a rooftop, resulting in the death of two individuals and injuries to twenty-six others. The prosecution alleged that the accused exhorted the main accused to fire at the supporters of the rival faction. The trial court and High Court examined the defense plea of self-defense, which was rejected due to the location of the firing and the lack of evidence supporting the claim. The Supreme Court upheld the conviction of the accused under Section 307 read with Section 34 IPC, while setting aside the conviction under Section 302.
